symptoms: In routine practice, dermatophytosis, also known as tinea and ringworm, is a fungal infection of the skin, that may affect skin, hair, and nails.
From a clinical perspective, typically it results in a red, itchy, scaly, circular rash.
In routine practice, hair loss may occur in the area affected.
From a clinical perspective, symptoms begin four to fourteen days after exposure.
From a clinical perspective, the types of dermatophytoses are typically named for the area of the body that they affect.
